findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom grant-type factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a provider-factory SPI implemented by extensions outside this repository. Adding getShortcut() as an abstract interface method makes every existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory fail to compile/load until it implements the new method. This should be a default method (for example returning a safe unknown shortcut or deriving one) so existing providers continue to work, with built-in factories overriding it.

findings.title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
findings.body: The previously public Context(Context) copy constructor has been deleted as a side effect of adding grantType capture. Custom grant types and token-exchange code compiled against the old SPI may use that constructor to clone/wrap a grant context; removing it is a binary- and source-incompatible API break unrelated to encoding token IDs. The copy constructor should be retained and updated to also copy grantType.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted and off-by-one grant check
findings.body: For an encoded prefix such as 'onrtac', the two grant characters are at indexes 4-5 ('ac'), but the matcher extracts substring(3, 5) ('ta'). It also returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. Because of the off-by-one extraction it will essentially never equal a real shortcut, so the equality branch is never taken and the matcher accepts access-token IDs with any grant type as long as the suffix is a UUID. The updated event assertions therefore cannot catch tokens encoded with the wrong grant.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: Line 72 checks grantType and line 73 checks grantType again with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'; rawTokenId itself is never null-checked. A null rawTokenId is accepted and later produces an encoded ID ending in ':null' from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId instead of failing fast at construction.

findings.title: Startup fails with opaque NPE if a grant factory returns no shortcut
findings.body: postInit unconditionally puts gtf.getShortcut() as a key into ConcurrentHashMap grantsByShortcuts (and as a value in grantsToShortcuts). A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning null - easy to do when stubbing the newly required method, and not prohibited by the interface contract - causes a NullPointerException during provider post-initialisation, preventing startup rather than a clear configuration error or a fallback to the unknown grant encoding. Null/duplicate shortcut validation should be explicit here.
